cells.value: Schema: core - prepared 07 Nov 2026 from the seed SQL ('167430e9-attachment.txt') and 'Prajwal_Table_Actions_Review' with the DB review fixes applied

Every table, column and allowed value of Prajwal's 5 tables: connection_intents, connection_requests, blocks, user_pseudonyms, profile_media. Other members' tables are not included. The seed data is on the last five tabs as supplied (before the fixes).
New or modified compared with the seed SQL and base file. The 'Change' column says exactly what changed. Removed items are listed in 'Values Not Kept'.
Tables -> Data Dictionary (every column) -> Value Lists (table > column > values; the 110 intents are grouped by category) -> Relationships.
Every user reference is <column> UUID REFERENCES core.users(user_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT. core.users belongs to the identity team. The seed still uses TEXT slugs - see Open Items.

ON DELETE RESTRICT everywhere. Columns, types and rules come from the reviewed data dictionary and the Table Actions Review; status and type lists are named CHECKs. No CREATE TABLE text was supplied, so constraint details are taken from those two files. Dropped values are in Values Not Kept.
PK = primary key. FK = link to another table. UNIQUE = no duplicates. CHECK = rule the database enforces.
What changed from the original workbook
Review fixes applied in this dictionary.
connection_intents (110 seeded rows), connection_requests (15), blocks (15), user_pseudonyms (7), profile_media (10). Reviewed against the Table Actions Review and the seed SQL.
connection_intents: created_at, updated_at. blocks: id, expires_at. profile_media: media_id, sort_order, purged_at. (connection_requests gets id in place of request_id.)
UUID, FK -> core.users(user_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT: sender, recipient, blocker, blocked, pseudonym user, media user. The seed used TEXT slugs such as aarav_sharma.

request_id (req001) -> id BIGINT identity, so core.connections.created_from_request_id can use the same type. UNIQUE (sender_user_id, idempotency_key); one pending request per sender-recipient pair; reverse pending request accepted instead.
category: 5 canonical values only. source_context: 5 values (replaces source_channel). status: 6 values. responded_at only when not pending; expires_at default 30 days; cooldown_until set on decline.
One active block per directed pair (partial UNIQUE where removed_at IS NULL); block_type, source, source_context and reason_code as named CHECKs; PK is a generated id.
pseudonym_id pd_001 -> UUID. One handle per row (3 seed rows held two). UNIQUE (scope, handle); one active default per user and scope; rotated_at tied to status.
Several media per user (media_id + sort_order); opaque object keys; moderation default pending; lifecycle checks on deleted_at / purged_at / purge_after.
Lookup table with PK intent_code; category (5 codes) and status as named CHECKs; sort_order restarts in each category. intent_id from the seed is kept as UNIQUE.
blocks: (blocker_user_id, blocked_user_id) WHERE removed_at IS NULL. user_pseudonyms: (scope, handle). profile_media: object_key. The seed SQL still uses blocker_user_id and user_id alone.
Kept from the seed and the action list although the final dictionary does not list it. Needs confirmation (Open Items).
request_id, pd_NNN IDs, and columns of the base file that are in neither the final dictionary nor the seed (see 'Values Not Kept').
connection_requests.category keeps 5 values; the longer taxonomy list (including dating / romance) is not stored.
50-code block reason list, overlapping reason / intent codes and 6 mismatched intent labels are not changed - they wait for approval (Open Items).
